item.title: How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
item.description: The death penalty is back in the news after Christa Pike survived two lethal injection attempts in Tennessee - but how widely used is it in the US?

item.title: Newly released video shows Luigi Mangione’s arrest
item.description: The bodycam footage also shows a police officer finding a gun in Mangione's backpack, days after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.

item.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
item.description: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.

item.title: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
item.description: The Latin American country will vote for its next president, as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.

item.title: Rare tornado whips through small Australian town
item.description: The twister was caught on camera in Ulladulla, New South Wales, damaging property and downing trees.

item.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
item.description: For the first time in three decades there has not been a single Atlantic hurricane in September, normally the most active month.

item.title: Why pastors may not be seen - or heard - preaching on Ghana's buses for much longer
item.description: Ghana is a predominantly Christian country where preaching on public transport is widespread.

item.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.

item.title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
item.description: They are accused of selling at least one student derivatives of kratom, often called "gas station heroin" in the US.

item.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
item.description: Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations of a woman who says she was drugged and gang raped as "deeply disturbing".

item.title: Debris found from plane that went missing off US coast
item.description: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.

item.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
item.description: More than 50 protests took place on Saturday after the government failed to get emergency legislation through parliament.

item.title: What to know about Brazil's election as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off
item.description: Polls suggest the election will be a closely run contest between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing rival.

item.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
item.description: State police and the country's security agency are looking into the co-pilot, who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel.

item.title: US Marine arrested over murder of woman in Okinawa, Japan
item.description: Japan's government lodged a formal protest with the US, demanding that military officials take action.

item.title: Indian police accused of sexually harassing journalists at protest
item.description: The allegations were made after police detained dozens of protesters demanding the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter rolls.

item.title: Christa Pike's prognosis still unclear after failed execution, lawyer says
item.description: Pike's lawyer says doctors are still trying to clear two lethal doses of pentobarbital from her body.

item.title: Ethiopian rebel forces withdraw from Tigray regional capital
item.description: Two residents in Mekelle tell the BBC pro-government forces have taken control of the city.

item.title: Polls close in Brazil as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remain neck and neck
item.description: If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.

item.title: Yemen's government announces all-out war to reclaim land from Houthis
item.description: The Yemeni president's announcement comes amid an exchange of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition.

item.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
item.description: BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near Kyiv's Northern Bridge, which has been hit for the second day in a row.

item.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
item.description: Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.
